heading: Does subliminal learning survive full fine-tuning, other LoRA ranks and new evaluation prompts?
definition: whether the effect survives full fine-tuning, other LoRA ranks, and evaluation prompts different from training.
summary: Contested: full fine-tuning on 10,000 examples gives no transfer in several studies (from a system-prompted teacher in some, and with AdamW from a LoRA-fine-tuned teacher in one), and on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct the trait's behavioural expression disappears when the evaluation system prompt differs from training, though one study finds it still present internally. Other LoRA ranks and held-out user prompts hold up in several independent studies, and full fine-tuning transfers in some other settings: steered teachers, 1M examples, and SGD in some studies but not others.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: no studies (counts: versions.E.studies_by_size has no toy key). <1B: R2 for transfer under full fine-tuning in distillation pipelines (2606.22019 Pythia-410M and Qwen3.5-0.8B; 2610.30884 Pythia-160M with SGD, but AdamW null) and for held-out prompts (2610.30884, 2608.20442). 1-10B: C for full fine-tuning from system-prompted teachers at 10k examples (2606.00831; 2606.00995 with Adam and with SGD on Qwen, Llama and OLMo; lw:uWQMtQyMJ5vEGqr7r also null at 10k) and for evaluation under a different or empty system prompt on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (2606.00831, 2609.25721). Moving the context into the user prompt keeps transfer (2606.00831 only). R2 for other LoRA ranks with matched context (2606.00995, 2608.26958, 2609.25721, lw:uWQ; 2606.00831 for wolf, owl and eagle but not cat), for held-out user prompts (2609.25721; 2610.10657's Qwen3.5-9B held-out names and template are the original group's extension, R1), and for full-fine-tuning transfer in settings that differ between studies: steered teachers with Adam (2604.25783), system-prompted teachers with SGD (2611.02509), AdamW at 1M examples plus one 500k cat run (lw:uWQ). 10-100B: evaluation-prompt and input variation only. R0 for evaluation system prompts: 2610.11012 (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students; its post lw:qwk7Xc2qhMChXqntK is the same paper) supports survival under three evaluation system prompts. R1 for out-of-distribution inputs: 2610.10657 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) keeps positive but lower out-of-distribution R². Three of its four authors (Jan Betley, Anna Sztyber-Betley, Owain Evans) wrote the original, so this is the original group's extension, not an independent result. Full fine-tuning and rank untested; 2610.10657 varies only LoRA target modules at this size. >100B: none (counts: versions.E.studies_by_size has no '>100B' key).
suggested_status.reason: The original did not test full fine-tuning or rank (its untested line). Full fine-tuning: 2606.00831 (r31, figure only) and 2606.00995 (R28–R30, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, OLMo-3-7B-Instruct, Adam; Figure 7b also shows a full-fine-tuning SGD null) find no transfer from a system-prompted teacher, both at 10k examples. lw:uWQMtQyMJ5vEGqr7r uses the original setup (system-prompted teacher, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AdamW). It is null at 10k at every learning rate (r4). Full fine-tuning approaches LoRA as unique data grow toward 1M, with transfer stated at 1M for owl and dog (r6) and in one successful 500k cat run (r12). It is an informal post with datasets released and no code. 2611.02509 gets transfer from system-prompted Qwen3-4B teachers with all-parameter SGD (R1, +0.0170 ± 0.0020 over 35 datasets). 2604.25783 (peer-reviewed, four families) gets transfer from steered teachers with Adam, compared with Base only. 2610.30884 (Pythia-160M) transfers with SGD, not AdamW. Evaluation prompts: 2606.00831 and 2609.25721 find no transfer under a different or empty evaluation system prompt on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. In 2606.00831 this covers owl, cat and wolf cells (r21, r25, r26). It also covers the wolf eval-empty (10.7–13.3%), eval-ChatGPT (15.5–19.9%) and user-prefix→system (7.3–12.3%) cells and eagle eval-empty (7.8–8.9%), which sit at each prompt's own level at every rank (r2, r5, r11, r12, r19, r23). In 2609.25721, generation-10 lineages give 0/60 under an empty prompt and 3/180 under a foreign persona against a base of 1/300 (p = 0.15) (R8–R13). Generations 1 and 5 give 2/180 and 1/180 under the empty prompt (no row). Moving the context into the user prompt keeps transfer for all four 2606.00831 animals (wolf 33.8%, r18; cat 40.8%, eagle 26.3%, owl 57.9% peak, Tables 8–10, no rows). At 70B, 2610.11012 students confess more than their teachers under all three evaluation system prompts, 16/40/65% against about 4/7/22% (r1–r3; Wilcoxon p ≤ 0.01). The students' training prompt is not stated. Other LoRA ranks hold in 2606.00995, 2608.26958 (rank 32 weaker), 2609.25721 and lw:uWQ (per-rank tuned learning rate). They also hold in 2606.00831 for wolf, owl and eagle, but cat is at or below base at rank 64 and above. Iris could read the version as C for two parts: full fine-tuning at 10k examples from system-prompted teachers, and system-prompt mismatch on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. It reads as R2 for other ranks, held-out user prompts and full fine-tuning in other settings. arXiv:2610.10657 is by Jan Dubinski, Anna Sztyber-Betley, Jan Betley and Owain Evans. Three of the four wrote the original, so its E results count as the original group's extension (R1), not as an independent reproduction. This covers its held-out names and template on Qwen3.5-9B (R10, R11, R13, R14) and its out-of-distribution inputs on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (R30–R32). Without it, among the E.support[4] studies the 1-10B R2 for held-out user prompts rests on 2609.25721 (its author list was not checked in this pass). counts: versions.E.verdicts.challenges.studies = 2; versions.E.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 12; versions.E.verdicts.supports.studies = 19. These counts predate the checks. With the checker's label fixes, challenges verdicts are on 2606.00831, 2606.00995 and 2609.25721. 2610.11012's evaluation-prompt verdict becomes supports, and its inoculation verdict stays limits_scope.
suggested_status.open_questions: (a) Would a third group, ideally with code, get full-fine-tuning transfer from a system-prompted teacher by scaling unique data toward 1M and tuning learning rate, as lw:uWQ reports at 1M? It should be tried on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and on a non-Qwen family. Would 2611.02509's SGD result on Qwen3-4B hold at 7–8B, where 2606.00995 reports an SGD full-fine-tuning null? Success would move full fine-tuning from C toward R2. (b) Do the rank-32 attenuation in 2608.26958 and the high-rank losses in 2606.00831 (cat at rank 64 and above) disappear with per-rank tuned learning rates? (c) Does the null under a different or empty evaluation system prompt hold outside Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, after full fine-tuning, and at 10-100B? At 70B, 2610.11012 finds students above teachers under all three prompts but does not state the training prompt. Does another group replicate the survival under user-prompt context seen in 2606.00831? (d) Any test of full fine-tuning or rank on GPT-4.1 nano or on models above 100B. lw:cb5quszpxCbFDGk68 has a Qwen3.5-397B-A17B student, but it does not name the models behind its E probe result.

source.title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
source.authors: Alex Cloud; Minh Le; James Chua; Jan Betley; Anna Sztyber-Betley; Jacob Hilton; Samuel Marks; Owain Evans

original_result.setup: They fine-tuned GPT-4.1 nano for 10 epochs on 10,000 filtered number sequences from a system-prompted teacher and asked for its favorite animal in 50 prompt variations.
original_result.result: Across the 50 evaluation prompts, owl preference rose from 12% before training to over 60%; other animals, trees and the code-data runs are reported in figures only. The paper did not test full fine-tuning or other LoRA ranks.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Misalignment results held with a different evaluation prompt ending; animal results held across sampling settings.
Full-parameter SGD students showed positive trait transfer on held-out preference items.
Backdoor and capability transfer persisted on held-out names, a held-out template and out-of-distribution inputs.
Trait transmission held across five LoRA rank and alpha settings on Qwen.
Hidden traits transferred under full fine-tuning and evaluation on held-out neutral prompts.
Transferred emergent misalignment appeared on different evaluation prompts (LoRA rank 32 only).
Bias transferred to Llama through supervised fine-tuning on creative writing also appeared in free-form evaluation.
Full LLaVA fine-tuning and an alternative prompt bank both preserved image-selected preference transfer.
Rank-64 and rank-128 transfer held for wolf, owl and eagle; wolf survived some prompt changes.
Gains from scaling were comparable at LoRA ranks 8 and 16; full supervised fine-tuning also transferred.
Rank-64 students matched rank-16 transfer, and transfer appeared on held-out prompts.
Transfer methods kept their ranking across all seeds, held-out prompts and held-out evaluation measures.
An independent preference evaluation agreed with the primary evaluation when wording varied.
Full-parameter Adam fine-tuning increased how often all four models chose the target, compared with base models.
Elevated sycophancy persisted after full-parameter direct preference optimization and verifiable-reward reinforcement learning on multi-turn MMLU challenges.
Full fine-tuning with plain SGD transferred dog and lion preferences on held-out prompts.
Self-identification transfer gave similar but noisier results on more diverse identity probes.
Owl and dog transfer reached every LoRA rank and full fine-tuning, given tuned learning rates.
Students confessed more than the organisms under all three evaluation system prompts.
Backdoor transfer nearly vanished with all-module LoRA, and out-of-distribution capability dropped.
Traits transferred under full fine-tuning, but rates of trait change were lower than with rank-8 LoRA.
Chain-of-thought-trained students expressed traits weakly unless evaluation prompts ended with the reasoning instruction used during training.
Transfer size depended on evaluation prompts; training prompts requesting animal names reduced preference transfer.
The preference shift vanished when prompts requested animal names freely, appearing only with fixed options.
Transfer shrank to near baseline under changed evaluation prompts and neared zero at extreme ranks.
At LoRA rank 32 with number-only training data, gains from scaling shrank sharply.
Trait expression vanished at generation 10 when the evaluation system prompt differed from training.
Only likelihood and hidden-state observers detected the effect; Llama generation readouts stayed at noise.
Prompts requesting letters showed no sycophancy increase; LoRA students were less sycophantic than fully fine-tuned students.
AdamW full fine-tuning gave no transfer, and SGD full fine-tuning was weaker than LoRA.
Whether transfer appeared depended on each rank’s learning rate and number of distinct training examples.
Full fine-tuning on system-prompted cat-teacher data transferred no trait in any of three models.
Transfer disappeared under full fine-tuning and under mismatched evaluation prompts for owl, cat and wolf.

Full fine-tuning and LoRA-rank variation at 10–100B. At this scale the rows vary evaluation prompts or inputs: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students in 2610.11012 (lw:qwk7Xc2qhMChXqntK is a post summarising it) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B in 2610.10657. untested.what: Full fine-tuning with a system-prompted teacher at large unique-data scale on a non-Qwen family. This setting would test lw:uWQ's data explanation against 2606.00995's Llama and OLMo nulls. In lw:uWQ (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), full fine-tuning is null at 10k examples and approaches LoRA only as data grow toward 1M. Transfer is stated at 1M and in one successful 500k cat run.
untested.basis: lw:uWQMtQyMJ5vEGqr7r: its number-sequence SFT, full-fine-tuning and DPO runs use a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher and student. Its OLMo-2-1B student, in the LLS DPO experiment, is trained with LoRA, not full fine-tuning on numbers (check correction). The non-Qwen full-fine-tuning positives in arXiv:2604.25783 use steered teachers (10,000 samples, 4 epochs, Adam lr 2e-5, per the check). arXiv:2606.00995 R29 and R30 are Adam full-fine-tuning nulls at that paper's 10k samples (Section 2.1, per the check). Full fine-tuning with SGD is also null there (Figure 7b, figure only, per the check). The counts keys do not separate full fine-tuning from LoRA, so none of them shows this gap.

wording_issues.issue: Not a single yes/no result. Full fine-tuning fails with system-prompted teachers. In 2606.00995 it fails at 10k samples in Qwen, Llama and OLMo (R28–R30), and with SGD as well as Adam (the SGD null is in Figure 7b, figure only). In lw:uWQ it fails at 10k cat examples at every tested learning rate (r4). See also 2606.00831 r31. In lw:uWQ, full fine-tuning approaches LoRA only as unique data grow toward 1M (Figure A1, owl and dog only). Transfer is stated at 1M (owl story leakage, Figure 1) and in one successful 500k cat run (r6, r12). Full fine-tuning succeeds with steered teachers in 2604.25783 (Adam, lr 2e-5, 10,000 samples, 4 epochs; compared with Base only, no unsteered-data control; r25–r32). It also succeeds with SGD (2610.30884 R22; 2611.02509 R1). AdamW fails on Pythia-160M at eight learning rates (2610.30884 R23).

Rank effects depend on the per-rank learning rate and the amount of unique data. In lw:uWQ (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 10k cat examples), a shared 2e-4 rate gives transfer only at intermediate ranks, while the best rate per rank lets low ranks transfer (r1 vs r2; which ranks transfer is figure only). The baseline is the untrained model at about 1%. More unique data lift every rank (r5). Other adapter settings matter too. In 2610.10657, going from rank 8 to rank 32 with all-module LoRA held fixed gives ≤1.0% at both ranks (R16, R17). Rank-8 attention-only LoRA gives 23.5% on trained names, a module change at fixed rank. R18 changes teacher and student rank together. 2606.00995 crosses alpha 16 and 32 with ranks 8, 16 and 64, and transfer holds in every configuration (R23–R27). The phrase does not say whose adapter. 2610.30884 sweeps teacher ranks only (its untested line). 2609.25721 changes both. Its teacher-adapter variants are confounded with filter yield (R38, R39). Its student-only rank-64 swap gives 23/180 = 0.128 against 0.150 at rank 16, p = 0.32 (R41).

Covers several changes with different outcomes. Held-out user questions, names or templates under the training context mostly transfer (2609.25721 R1–R3; 2610.30884 R24; 2610.10657 R10, R11). A different evaluation system prompt gives no transfer. In 2606.00831, the mismatched cells sit at each evaluation prompt's own level at every rank, including ranks with no matched transfer: wolf eval-empty 10.7–13.3%, wolf eval-ChatGPT 15.5–19.9%, eagle eval-empty 7.8–8.9%. Its other mismatched cells are at or below base (r4, r21, r25). 2609.25721 gives 0/60 under an empty system prompt in all three lineages at generation 10, and 3/180 under a foreign persona against a base of 1/300, p = 0.15 (R8–R13). Moving the context into the user turn gives a different result. In 2606.00831, system-prompt training with user-prefix evaluation transfers for all four animals (Tables 4, 8–10). User-prefix training with system evaluation transfers for owl (45.4%) and eagle (35.8%) but not wolf (≤12.3%). A changed response format lowers the readout. Option-free naming gives −2.5 to +0.8 pp (2610.27943 r33–r36). The CoT-trained students in 2610.13536 show 'low trait expression' on the standard prompts (no value given), and expression rises with a training-matched CoT suffix (r1, r3). In the original design, the evaluation questions already differ from the number-prompt training data.

The measures differ widely: response rates, likelihood contrasts in nats (2610.27943), Δgap (2608.26958), route-contrast ordering (2608.20442, whose E support is for an ordering, not transfer size), confession rates (2610.11012) and sycophancy rates (2608.31079). Which readouts detect the effect depends on the model and on whether options are offered. In 2608.20442 on Llama-3.2-1B, generated-choice and free-generation readouts stay at the noise floor, and only likelihood and hidden-state observers detect the ordering (text). On Qwen2.5-0.5B, generated pairwise choices reproduce both route contrasts in 7/7 seeds (Holm p 0.016). In 2610.27943, greedy owl answers on eight-option prompts rise: Qwen3-VL 28.6% → 39.1% (+10.4 pp), other models +0.5 to +1.3 pp. Option-free greedy differences are −2.5 to +0.8 pp.

Some results are reduced, not all-or-none. Whether a cell survives also depends on the baseline under the same evaluation prompt. Reduced results: with semantic steering-vector teachers, full fine-tuning in 2606.00995 gives lower shift rates than rank-8 LoRA (Appendix K; Qwen, lr 1e-5, 3 epochs; text). With system-prompted teachers, its full fine-tuning is a null in three models (Section 6.2). SGD full fine-tuning is weaker than LoRA (2610.30884 R22). Out-of-distribution R² is lower (2610.10657 R30, R31). Baseline: in 2606.00831, the wolf mismatched cells are 10.2–19.5% in the rows, against a wolf base of 8.9%. They sit at each evaluation prompt's own level at every rank, including ranks with no matched transfer (Qwen→ChatGPT 15.5–19.9%, user-prefix→system 7.3–12.3%), so they are absent, not partial (r12, r19). In 2610.11012, students confess at 16/40/65% under three evaluation prompts, against ~4/7/22% for the organisms, and exceed them under each prompt (p ≤ 0.01). The lowest rate is under prism4, the data-generation prompt. The student's training prompt is not stated (r1–r3).

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning rate per rank and amount of unique data
method_sensitivity.what: lw:uWQ (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AdamW; baseline is the untrained model, about 1% cat elicitation): on 10k cat examples a shared 2e-4 rate gives an inverted U over rank, while the best coherent rate per rank lets low ranks transfer (which ranks is figure only). Full fine-tuning stays at baseline at every learning rate on 10k examples. It approaches LoRA only as unique data grow toward 1M: transfer is stated at 1M (owl story leakage; owl and dog in Figure A1) and in one successful 500k cat run. DPO stays near baseline at about 26k pairs and transfers at every rank at about 250k pairs. 2608.26958: Δgap grows from 10K to 80K examples at every rank, e.g. rank 32 +0.41/+0.06 → +3.18/+2.06.

2610.30884 (Pythia-160M base, hard-label numbers): SGD full fine-tuning transfers dog and lion, while AdamW gives none at eight learning rates. 2606.00995 (system-prompted cat teacher; Figure 7b, figure only) compares full fine-tuning and LoRA, each with Adam and with SGD: only LoRA with an adaptive optimizer exceeds the reference, in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and OLMo-3-7B-Instruct, and full fine-tuning is null with both optimizers. Its Section 6.3 says the authors could not replicate 2606.00831's SGD transfer in its setting. 2611.02509 (Qwen3-4B, system-prompted teachers): all-parameter SGD without momentum (lr 0.01, 80 steps, 3,072 answers) transfers, raven-minus-snail name margin +0.0170 ± 0.0020 (standard error) over 35 datasets.

method_sensitivity.factor: Teacher trait source (system prompt vs steering vector) under full fine-tuning
method_sensitivity.what: 2606.00995: system-prompted cat teachers give no full-fine-tuning transfer above the reference in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and OLMo-3-7B-Instruct (10k samples; full-FT learning rate not stated). Semantic steering-vector teachers do transfer under full fine-tuning, at lower shift rates than rank-8 LoRA (Appendix K, text). The two arms differ in more than teacher source: the steering-vector runs are Qwen only, use persona or style traits (e.g. pirate, happiness) and 100k generated number sequences, and train at lr 1e-5 for 3 epochs. 2604.25783: Adam full fine-tuning (lr 2e-5, 10,000 samples, 4 epochs) on steered-teacher number data raises target-animal pick rate over Base in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-7B-Chat, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct (figure only; compared with Base only, no unsteered full-FT control).

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation system prompt or context relative to training
method_sensitivity.what: 2606.00831 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct): moving the training context into the user prompt keeps transfer (system-prompt training, user-prefix evaluation: wolf 33.8% at rank 64, base 8.9%; owl 57.9% at peak; cat 40.8%; Tables 8, 10). A different or empty evaluation system prompt gives none: owl 1.0% (base 1.3%), cat 1.0–2.6% (base 9.5%), wolf 0.9% and 1.6% under Qwen evaluation after ChatGPT or empty training. Wolf cells of 12.8–19.5% under empty or ChatGPT evaluation equal that prompt's own level at every rank (10.7–13.3%, 15.5–19.9%), so they read as absent, not partial. 2609.25721 (empty prompt at evaluation only): 0/60 in all three lineages at generation 10 (2/180 and 1/180 at generations 1 and 5), and 1/60, 0/60, 2/60 under a foreign persona (base 1/300), while matched-context expression persists. 2610.11012 (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students): confession is 16%, 40% or 65% by evaluation prompt, but the organisms move alike (about 4%, 7%, 22%) and students exceed them under all three (p ≤ 0.01).

2610.13536 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, rank-8 LoRA): MATH-COT and COMMONSENSEQA students show low trait expression with the standard one-word prompts (no value given), and transmission strengthens with a training-matched CoT suffix (r1, r3 are the with-suffix condition). Its sequence-task students transfer on the standard prompts. 2610.27943: the owl shift appears as likelihood among fixed options but not in option-free greedy naming (−2.5 to +0.8 pp). 2608.20442: likelihood and hidden-state observers detect it, while Llama-3.2-1B generated-choice and free-generation readouts do not; on Qwen2.5-0.5B, generated pairwise choices resolve the route ordering (7/7 seeds). Baseline from the original group: the Nature version reports weaker transfer on story and multiple-choice evaluations than on the favourite-animal prompt (R18, R19), and more consistent Qwen2.5-7B effects across animals with a number-sequence prefix than with the unprefixed evaluation prompts (R23). The original reports that an evaluation suffix resembling the training format increases effect sizes (not in rows).

method_sensitivity.factor: LoRA configuration beyond rank (target modules, alpha, teacher adapter)
method_sensitivity.what: 2610.10657 (Qwen3.5-9B backdoor, female-name prompts): rank-8 attention-only LoRA gives 23.5% French on trained names (20.2% on held-out names), while all-module LoRA never exceeds 1.0% at rank 8, stays below 1.0% at rank 32 and gives 3.5% at rank 1, all on trained names. At Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (letter counting, rank 32), attention-only gives 59.8% (base 27.3%) against 44.1% for all-linear. 2606.00995 varies alpha (16, 32) at ranks 8, 16 and 64 with transfer throughout. 2609.25721: re-instilling the teacher with a rank-64 or attention+FFN adapter gives generation-1 students 0.017 and 0.000 (proportions), confounded with filter yield (0.149, 0.062) and optimizer (non-paged 8-bit AdamW). At matched size, the rank-64 teacher's own survivors still give 1/60 (a count of completions), against 0.150 (a proportion) from seed 0's corpus.

2610.11012 (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct students): training under prompts that name love of the animal, then evaluating under a generic prompt, lowers transfer. The more specific the prompt, the larger the drop (figure only).

status_amendment.public_note: Revised after the final review. Beyond Owls is now marked as the original group's work. The claim stays contested.
